blurb:
If you've got a game to watch or just want to sit outside and not think too hard about life for a few hours, The Wing Cafe and Tap House on Roswell Road is a solid call. High energy, outdoor tiki bar, craft beer, live music on the weekends. It's a place built for hanging out, not rushing through.

The wings are the main event here, obviously. With over 1,900 reviews sitting at 4.4 stars, people are not showing up for the ambiance alone. Order the wings, grab something on tap, and let the afternoon go.

It runs all seven days from 11am to 11pm, so there's almost no bad time to pop in.

blurb:
Hamp & Harry's is the kind of spot I keep coming back to on the Square. It's got that easy, comfortable energy where you're not underdressed and you're not overdressed, and the service actually feels like people want to be there. Good for brunch on the weekend or a casual lunch if you're already in the Marietta area.

The fried chicken biscuit is what gets ordered around here, and for good reason. The biscuit is hot, fluffy, and big enough that taking half of it home is a real possibility. The salad dressing is one of those things you don't expect to notice but definitely do.

Just keep in mind they're closed Mondays, so don't plan a long weekend brunch run and show up to a locked door.

blurb:
JJ's is tucked into a strip on Roswell Road and I'll be honest, it took me too long to try it. Once you do, you kind of kick yourself for waiting. It's a no-fuss pizza place that punches way above its weight. Good for a weeknight dinner with the family, a game day pickup, or just when you want pizza that actually tastes like pizza.

Get the garlic cheese knots. Full stop. The stuffed pizza is worth ordering too, and it's one of those things that sounds simple but delivers more than you expect. My wife and I have done both and left happy every time.

They're closed Tuesdays, so keep that in mind if you're planning a midweek pizza night.

blurb:
Ray's on the River is where my wife and I go when we want a real night out. Not a birthday dinner at a chain restaurant, an actual special occasion. Sitting along the Chattahoochee with elevated Southern seafood on the table in front of you is a hard experience to beat. It earns every bit of its reputation, and over 11,000 reviews at 4.6 stars doesn't happen by accident.

The menu leans into Southern coastal flavors done well. It's the restaurant version of a slow Sunday, meaning you're not in a hurry and you shouldn't be. Show up ready to take your time.

Sunday hours run a split schedule, open for brunch in the morning and then back open for dinner in the evening, so check the hours before you head out if Sunday is your day.

blurb:
Heirloom Market BBQ is a tiny place off Akers Mill with one communal table and a lineup of barbecue that has people driving across town for it. The twist here is the Korean-Southern BBQ crossover, and it works better than it has any right to. At 4.7 stars across more than 3,000 reviews, this place has clearly figured something out.

The BBQ is the draw, full stop. The slight Asian accent on the menu sets it apart from every other smokehouse in the area. If you've never tried Korean-inflected smoked meat, this is worth making the trip for.

They're only open Tuesday through Saturday, and they close at 8pm. Show up early because this is not a big room and they do run out of things.
